PullRequest.Title: agentHost: stabilize trusted Codex workspace hooks
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- recheck Codex workspace hook trust after provisional thread startup, when a cold app-server has populated its hook catalog
- carry newly discovered trust directly into a lossless pre-turn replacement thread
- repeat a cold resume when hooks become visible only after the initial resume
- distinguish hook discovery failures from an empty catalog so failures do not trigger unnecessary restarts
- wait for the integration test Workspace Trust update before creating its session

## Motivation

A cold Codex process can return an empty `hooks/list` result before its first thread starts. The thread then starts without `hooks.state`, so a trusted workspace `SessionStart` hook does not run for the first turn. This is a product race that surfaced as a flaky timeout in Azure build 473928.

The separate quarantine PR is #336297. This change fixes the underlying product behavior and keeps the trusted integration case active.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- hygiene on all three changed files
- 17 focused workspace-hook-trust unit tests
- full Codex customizations integration suite: 6 passing
- trusted/untrusted integration pair repeated in five cold processes: 5/5 passing

## Review

Reviewed with Claude Opus. The review findings around inherited hooks, replacement connections, cold resume, discovery failure signaling, polling overhead, and send-path coverage were addressed before opening this draft.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Fresh or prewarmed Codex chat sends its first user turn in a trusted workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before turn/start can be issued, the send awaits materialization, then the added post-start hooks/list recheck. If grants changed, it also awaits thread/unsubscribe and replacement thread/start. Baseline checkpointing and later customization publication remain off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the cwd-scoped effective hook catalog via hooks/list after provisional thread startup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added request for the first turn of each trusted-workspace chat; zero for untrusted/no-cwd sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Materialization queried hooks/list before thread/start, but first send did not recheck it after startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized before turn/start and therefore adds one app-server round trip to first-turn latency

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe the provisional thread and start a replacement carrying newly discovered hook grants
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one replacement on this path when the post-start grant signature differs; no replacement on a warm unchanged catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hook discovery could not trigger a pre-turn replacement; restarts occurred only for changed tools, MCP, or customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized before turn/start only in the cold late-discovery case

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: App-server hook discovery underlying the cwd-scoped hooks/list catalog request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cwd catalog per request; no host-side per-hook filesystem calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The catalog was queried during materialization, not re-queried after provisional startup on first send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transitively contributes to the awaited hooks/list duration

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One recheck per chat before its first successful turn; the request is cwd-scoped to one primary working directory, not per hook or per workspace root. Hook result processing scales linearly with the returned catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Materialization is coalesced by session.materializePromise. The added hook recheck is sequential on the first-send path; normal host turn handling drains queued user messages after the active turn, so this does not create aggregate per-item fan-out. Different chats can progress independently as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An untrusted or missing cwd short-circuits without IPC. Trusted workspaces query the app-server catalog even when a prewarm populated it; warm catalogs avoid replacement when the signature matches. There is no host cache because Workspace Trust and hook hashes must be current; pending trust is consumed and cleared after replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the extra serialized IPC and conditional replacement: changed code and unit request-order assertions establish both cardinality and critical-path placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external app-server implementation and measured warm/cold hooks/list latency are not in this repository, so exact milliseconds are unknown. The added round trip is one-time per chat and specifically required to observe a catalog that becomes available only after startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR deliberately adds one bounded post-start recheck to repair cold catalog discovery, avoids replacement when the signature is unchanged, short-circuits untrusted workspaces, and clears pending state. This is an intentional one-time correctness tradeoff rather than scaling or repeated per-turn work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A restored Codex session resumes on a cold or warm app-server
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resume preparation performs the existing initial hooks/list before thread/resume. When that result contains no eligible grants, the changed path awaits one post-resume hooks/list; only newly discovered grants cause thread/unsubscribe and a second thread/resume. MCP inventory refresh after successful resume remains fire-and-forget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial thread/resume using the pre-resume hook trust snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per restored session, unchanged except that it may be followed by a bounded retry
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One thread/resume was issued after one pre-resume hooks/list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required resume boundary on the send/restore critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-query hooks/list after an empty-grant initial resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one added request per resume attempt whose initial eligible grant set is empty
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized after initial resume and before the session is considered resumed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unsubscribe and resume the thread again with late-discovered grants
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one added unsubscribe and one added resume when the second query finds eligible grants
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial resume completed without a late-grant replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds two serialized round trips only in the cold late-discovery case

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: App-server hook catalog discovery behind the post-resume hooks/list request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cwd catalog query in the empty-grant fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the pre-resume hook catalog was queried.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One restored thread at a time per session; the added fallback is one cwd-scoped catalog request when initial eligible grant count is zero, plus one replacement resume only if late eligible project hooks appear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: session.resumePromise coalesces concurrent resume demand for the same session, and all hooks/list/resume/unsubscribe calls are serialized. Different restored sessions remain independent; no new shared burst is created by a single collection loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm catalog with eligible project hooks skips the second query. Empty/ineligible catalogs take one negative recheck because the first cold resume may populate project hooks; a second empty result is not retried in a loop. Failures return undefined and do not trigger replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: changed control flow and tests explicitly establish hooks/list, resume, hooks/list, unsubscribe, resume ordering, with no loop after the second resume.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog scan and resume costs are external and unmeasured here. The tests prove the maximum changed sequence but not production prevalence of cold empty catalogs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra work is bounded to the cold/negative-catalog recovery path, same-session resumes are coalesced, warm positive catalogs skip it, and no unbounded retry or fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Direct backing creation or fork applies workspace hook trust
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation builds one trust snapshot and awaits one hooks/list before thread/start or thread/fork. Trust context validation is synchronous and may rebuild only if Workspace Trust or cwd changes during the operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch hooks/list and then start or fork one Codex thread
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hooks/list plus one thread/start or thread/fork per operation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These operations already queried hooks/list and then started/forked a thread; the diff wraps grants with a context signature without increasing normal boundary count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cwd-scoped catalog per direct creation or fork; grant signature work scales linearly with the returned eligible hooks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each chat creation is serialized by _chatLifecycleSequencer for that chat. There is no new per-hook IPC and no changed global limiter behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No host cache is added; an untrusted cwd returns an empty snapshot without hooks/list. A context change invalidates the snapshot and can cause one fresh query before applying it, preserving authorization freshness.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that normal boundary cardinality is unchanged; changed call sites only pass cwd and validate the captured trust context.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A trust/cwd mutation during the small discovery-to-apply window can add a rebuild, but prevalence is low and bounded by user configuration changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: normal IPC count, cardinality, and serialization are unchanged, while added signatures are small bounded CPU/allocation work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Traced first-send, prewarm, cold resume, direct creation, and fork boundaries; considered repeated work, boundary fan-out, coalescing, cache lifecycle, retention, serialization, and concurrency. The PR adds bounded critical-path IPC for late hook discovery but gates retries/replacements, coalesces resume/materialization, and introduces no high-confidence actionable scaling regression.
